lede_html: We survey {papers} papers and place each method along the three axes of the Lenses section: the lens \(\lambda\) is the observation point, the variation \(Z\) is the resampling variable, and the auxiliary structure \(S\) is used to obtain the score.

items.title: Semantical estimators measure the spread of meanings
items.body_html: All semantical methods are native estimators that read a semantical observation and measure the spread of meanings. The relation \(R\) moves from cluster to graph to manifold, which weakens the assumptions on meaning. Verbalization branches off this line and lets the model itself judge meaning.

items.title: Distributional estimators as baselines
items.body_html: The distributional lens is the earliest and most studied lens, and its estimators are the usual baselines. Most methods read token probabilities with gray-box access, and black-box methods use sampled text or a proxy model. Most estimators are native. The surrogate estimators select or weight tokens with a semantics model to approximate the spread over meanings.

items.title: Representational estimators are mostly surrogates
items.body_html: All representational methods need white-box access, and most read a single forward pass and target correctness. The native estimators measure spread in hidden state space by a closed-form function or an unsupervised probe. The surrogate estimators fit a model against a semantical or distributional label.

items.title: Structural estimators often target grounding
items.body_html: All structural methods need white-box access, and some add cross-lens signals. The native estimators measure spread on the attention pattern. The surrogate estimators fit a model against correctness or grounding labels. Structural methods are more often used for grounding prediction than methods at the other lenses.
